answer: One concrete defense is to require every agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit in a shared vault before it can trade or vote. A single operator can spin up a fable of a thousand fake identities, but each copy must fund its own stake, so forging an army becomes as expensive as the influence it buys. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, like an ember that keeps glowing only while it is tended, while detected sybils lose their deposits, which are burned or redistributed to the victims. Cost, not identity checks, makes the attack unprofitable.
